subject: Clarify backup erasure sequencing, audit trail, and restore assurances
messages:
From: Elena Petrova <elena.petrova@globex.com>
To: stephanie_nguyen@redwood.com
Cc: IT Ops Team <it-ops@globex.com>, samuel.ortiz@globex.com
Date: Fri, 03 Mar 2028 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: Questions on backup erasure sequencing and audit trail guarantees

Hi Stephanie —

Thanks for the earlier call. Globex is finalizing its data residency and retention policy mapping for EU-regulated customers and we need a few clarifications on Redwood's backup and DR behavior before legal signs off. High level asks below, attached is our retention matrix.

1) If a customer issues a permanent deletion (remove all their records + legal hold cleared), what is the end-to-end timeline for: primary data deletion, backup snapshot removal, cross-region replica expunge, and garbage-collection tombstone finalization?

2) During the delete window, what vestiges remain accessible to Redwood staff (e.g., snapshots, debug copies, logs), and what controls exist to restrict access?

3) Can Redwood provide an audit trail for the delete operation across the whole lifecycle (request received, primaries deleted, snapshot marked for purge, replication tombstone time, and final expunge)? We need a CSV-style sample.

4) In case of a legal hold reversal within 30 days, what restore pathway exists and how many bytes/time to recover? Conversely, after final expunge, is recovery impossible?

We'd like a concise, firm timeline and an example audit CSV to attach to our compliance package. Can you confirm by end of week?

Best,
Elena
Head of Vendor Risk — Globex Financial
(Attachment: Globex-Retention-Requirements-2028.pdf)

From: stephanie_nguyen@redwood.com
To: Elena Petrova <elena.petrova@globex.com>
Cc: ben_carter@redwood.com, marissa_cole@redwood.com, dylan_brooks@redwood.com
Date: Fri, 03 Mar 2028 10:03:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Questions on backup erasure sequencing and audit trail guarantees

Hi Elena —

Thanks for the clear list. I'm looping in Ben (sales lead) and Marissa (infra/dr) to provide exact timings and the audit sample; Dylan will confirm the RBAC and access controls language. High level answers up front so you have something to include in the package while we pull the precise audit CSV:

- End-to-end timeline (typical): primary deletion processed within minutes of request; snapshot marking for purge within 24 hours; cross-region replica tombstone scheduled at next replication cycle (up to 48 hours); final background expunge (garbage collection) within 30–45 days by default depending on retention and retentionOverrides.
- Access during window: snapshots and logs are logically retained but access is strictly limited to authorized SRE and compliance engineers via IAM roles; all access is logged and requires justification for emergency retrieval.
- Audit trail: yes, we can provide a machine-readable audit CSV showing every step and actor.
- Restores: if you place a legal hold reversal within 30 days we can generally restore from a marked snapshot; after the final expunge the data is irrecoverable.

We'll follow up with a precise expunge SLA options (shorter windows available under Dedicated/Private contracts) and the sample audit export.

Action: Marissa, can you drop an example CSV and the exact timings for Private vs Hosted? Ben/dylan, any customer-facing wording changes?

Thanks —
Stephanie
VP, Sales Operations
Redwood Inference

From: marissa_cole@redwood.com
To: stephanie_nguyen@redwood.com, ben_carter@redwood.com
Cc: dylan_brooks@redwood.com
Date: Fri, 03 Mar 2028 13:18:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Questions on backup erasure sequencing and audit trail guarantees

Stephanie / team —

See notes below (I'll paste into a short CSV and send back to Elena). Numbers are conservative, we can offer tighter SLAs in Dedicated/Private agreements.

Timeline (Hosted API default tier):
- T+0 (request ingested): Deletion job queued; primary objects flagged and soft-deleted within 0–5 minutes.
- T+0 to T+24h: Snapshot lifecycle controller marks any incremental snapshots that reference deleted objects as "candidate for purge"; snapshot metadata retains a tombstone link.
- T+24 to T+72h: Cross-region replication observes tombstone and marks replicas for expunge (replication cycle dependent).
- T+30 to T+45 days: Background garbage collector finalizes expunge; object data blocks are eligible for physical overwrites; audit record shows final expunge timestamp.

Private/Dedicated options (contracted):
- Option A (30-day expedited expunge): final expunge 7–14 days after request.
- Option B (7-day expedited expunge): final expunge 3–7 days after request + attestation.

Access controls:
- Only users with role "sre:deletion-recovery" and "compliance:viewer" can view snapshot metadata; content retrieval requires an "emergency_access" ticket and is cryptographically gated via KMS policy.
- All accesses produce immutable audit events (actor, timestamp, IP, justification).

Restore path and limits:
- If legal hold reversed before final expunge, we restore from the latest consistent snapshot; restore time is proportional to dataset size (example: 100GB cold restore ~2–6 hours). After final expunge, recovery is impossible.

I'll attach a sample CSV and the CSV column definitions (request_id, actor, step, timestamp, snapshot_id, region, note).

—Marissa
Senior Infrastructure Engineer, Redwood Inference
(Attachment: sample-audit-trail.csv)

From: ben_carter@redwood.com
To: Elena Petrova <elena.petrova@globex.com>, stephanie_nguyen@redwood.com
Cc: marissa_cole@redwood.com, dylan_brooks@redwood.com
Date: Mon, 06 Mar 2028 11:26:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Questions on backup erasure sequencing and audit trail guarantees

Elena —

Adding a short customer-friendly summary for procurement / legal:

1) Default hosted behavior (guarantee): final expunge occurs within 30–45 days; we provide a complete audit trace from request through final expunge.
2) Contracted guarantees: Dedicated/Private customers can contract 3–14 day final-expunge SLAs and receive an attestation certificate upon completion.
3) Access & controls: snapshot content is cryptographically protected, role-gated, and access is logged; emergency retrieval requires approval workflow.

Next steps:
- Stephanie: can we confirm pricing delta for 14-day and 7-day expedited expunge?
- Marissa: confirm CSV export attached contains the column headers and a realistic row sample.

Happy to jump on a short legal call if needed.

Best,
Ben
Enterprise Sales — Redwood Inference

From: stephanie_nguyen@redwood.com
To: Elena Petrova <elena.petrova@globex.com>, IT Ops Team <it-ops@globex.com>, Samuel Ortiz <samuel.ortiz@globex.com>
Cc: ben_carter@redwood.com, marissa_cole@redwood.com, dylan_brooks@redwood.com
Date: Mon, 06 Mar 2028 16:41:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Questions on backup erasure sequencing and audit trail guarantees

Hi Elena / team —

Thanks for the patience. Attached are the files Marissa produced (sample audit CSV and column definitions) plus our short one-pager that maps Redwood retention primitives to Globex's matrix. Key points you can include in the compliance packet: 

• Hosted default expunge window: 30–45 days after deletion request (final expunge irrecoverable).
• Dedicated/Private contractual options: 3–14 day final expunge paths available with attestation.
• Restore: possible only if legal hold reversal occurs before final expunge; restore times depend on dataset size (we provided examples in the one-pager).
• Auditability: we provide machine-readable CSV with step-level records and an immutable event id for chain-of-custody.

Please find attached: Globex-Retention-Requirements-2028.pdf (your original), sample-audit-trail.csv, and a short mapping PDF. If you'd like, Ben and I can join your legal/procurement call on Thursday to walk through the contractual language.

Best regards,
Stephanie Nguyen
VP, Sales Operations
Redwood Inference
(Attachments: sample-audit-trail.csv, redwood-retention-mapping-2028.pdf)
